To exploit seasonality in the Indian equity market, we will focus on trading rules based on historical calendar effects. The economic mechanism involves analyzing patterns in stock prices around specific times of the year, such as festive seasons, election periods, or quarterly earnings releases. These events can influence investor behavior and market sentiment, leading to predictable price movements.

Seasonal trends persist due to consistent human behaviors and market expectations tied to these events. For example, certain sectors like retail might see increased trading volumes during Diwali, while others may benefit from government policies announced before elections.

The rule would identify key periods with historical outperformance and create a strategy to buy stocks in those sectors ahead of time and sell them after the positive price action has run its course. This could involve setting specific entry and exit points based on calendar dates or market indicators that signal the start and end of these beneficial seasons.

The signal for this systematic equity strategy would focus on identifying key seasonal periods in the Indian equity market. Daily signals are derived by analyzing historical stock price data (open, high, low, close) and volume over a lookback period of one year to identify sectors with consistent outperformance during specific seasons.

On each trading day, we rank stocks based on their performance metrics such as returns, volatility-adjusted returns, or volume changes relative to the same period in the previous years. Sectors showing historical outperformance are then prioritized for buying, while underperforming sectors may be candidates for selling.

The ranking is computed using a score that combines price momentum and volume increase around key events like Diwali, general elections, etc. Stocks with higher scores indicating stronger seasonal trends are selected as candidates for the long side of the portfolio, while those with lower or negative scores are considered for the short side.

This systematic strategy can hold up to 20-30 names in its portfolio, with weights allocated based on their score rankings. The top-ranked stocks receive higher weights, typically between 1% to 5%, ensuring diversification while capturing strong seasonal trends. Risk limits are set to prevent significant losses; the total position size does not exceed 5% of the portfolio value at any given time, and individual stock positions do not surpass 2% of the portfolio, with stop-loss orders in place to limit potential downside to no more than 10% of the investment capital.
